title: Trinidad and Tobago Owes Small Firms TT$899M in Overdue VAT Refunds | Across the Water, Ep. 25
lede: Trinidad and Tobago's government told the Senate on Nov 24 that 5,350 small and medium-sized businesses held VAT refund claims overdue beyond the six-month legal limit, worth an unaudited TT$898.7 million. It is one line in a wider arrears bill: TT$1.77 billion in fuel subsidies owed to National Petroleum and Unipet, and almost TT$20 billion in gas costs NGC is seeking from the state power utility, against public debt of 83.3% of GDP.
keyPoints: As of Sept 1, 2026, 5,350 SMEs had VAT refunds overdue beyond six months, an unaudited TT$898.7 million; the government targets a 25% cut by end-December (Senate, Nov 24, via Trinidad Guardian and TTT News).
General government debt is estimated at TT$149.54 billion, 83.3% of GDP, at the end of fiscal 2026; the revised fiscal 2026 deficit is TT$7 billion (Ministry of Finance via Trinidad Guardian).

The state owed National Petroleum TT$1.33 billion and Unipet TT$440 million in fuel subsidies at Oct 31; TT$450 million in cheques were prepared Nov 18; the opposition says arrears exceed TT$2 billion (Trinidad Express, TTT News).
NGC is seeking to recover almost TT$20 billion in gas costs from power utility T&TEC, first booked at TT$10 billion; its chairman says a decision comes before Dec 31 (Trinidad Guardian, Nov 20).
The fiscal 2027 budget projects revenue of TT$59.7 billion against spending of TT$63.4 billion, a TT$3.6 billion deficit, on oil at US$77 a barrel (Budget statement, Oct 12, 2026).
